channel.title: BRYME — writing opportunities, guides and verification
channel.description: Legitimate paid-writing opportunities, practical guides and BRYME's firsthand verification record.

item.title: Westerly: $250 per poem, $500 for prose, $620 for comics
item.description: Westerly, published twice a year out of the University of Western Australia, pays $250 for one poem, $300 for a poetic sequence, $500 for prose, $620 for

item.title: The /tEmz/ Review
item.description: The /tEmz/ Review pays $20 per prose piece and $20 per batch of poems.

item.title: The Rialto: £20 per poem on publication
item.description: The Rialto, a Norwich-based poetry magazine, pays £20 per poem on publication.

item.title: The New Quarterly: $400 for prose, $100 for poetry
item.description: The New Quarterly pays $400 for fiction and non-fiction pieces and $100 per poem.

item.title: The Malahat Review: CAD$70 per published page
item.description: The Malahat Review, based at the University of Victoria, pays CAD$70 per published page plus a one-year subscription and two copies.

item.title: The London Magazine: pays for everything published in print
item.description: The London Magazine, the UK's oldest literary magazine, pays a fee for everything it publishes in print but cannot currently pay for pieces published on the

item.title: The Fiction Desk
item.description: The Fiction Desk pays £25 per thousand words for short stories of 1,000–15,000 words in its print anthologies — £150 for a 6,000 word story.

item.title: Shoreline of Infinity
item.description: Shoreline of Infinity is a Scottish science fiction magazine paying £20 per 1,000 words for stories up to 6,000 words.

item.title: Propel Magazine: £20 honorarium, UK and Ireland poets only
item.description: Propel Magazine publishes poets based in the UK or Ireland who have not yet published a first full-length collection, paying a £20 honorarium.

item.title: PRISM international: $40 per page for prose, $45 for poetry
item.description: PRISM international, run out of UBC, pays $40 CAD per printed page for prose and $45 CAD per printed page for poetry, plus two contributor copies.

item.title: Prairie Fire: 10¢ per word for prose, $40 per poem
item.description: Prairie Fire, a Winnipeg quarterly, pays 10 cents per word for prose to a maximum of $250 per piece, and $40 per poem, plus a contributor's copy.

item.title: Poetry Wales poetry: £20 per poem, 2–3 windows a year
item.description: Poetry Wales pays £20 per poem. The poetry window opens 2–3 times a year and is capped at 550 submissions per issue.

item.title: Poetry Wales features: £150 per 3,000 words, rolling pitches
item.description: Poetry Wales has a rolling submissions window for features, articles and interviews, paid at £150 per 3,000 words or in that proportion.

item.title: Poetry London: £35 per poem, general submissions
item.description: Poetry London pays £35 per poem, with review and interview fees benchmarked at £50 per 1,000 words.

item.title: Pellicle pitching: £375–£675 per commissioned feature
item.description: Pellicle is a UK drinks magazine paying fixed commission fees — £375 for a 1,500–2,000 word feature, £525 for a long read, £675 for a photo essay.

item.title: Orion Magazine: $200 per poem, poetry call 10–15
item.description: Orion pays $200 for poems accepted into its Spring 2027 Memory and Place issue, with the call open 10–15 September 2026 or until 800 submissions arrive.

item.title: One Story: $500 for a single short story
item.description: One Story publishes exactly one story per issue and pays $500 plus 25 contributor copies. It takes literary fiction of 3,000–8,000 words.

item.title: Mslexia: pays for every piece published, women writers only
item.description: Mslexia is a magazine for women's writing that pays for every piece it publishes.

item.title: Modern Poetry in Translation
item.description: Modern Poetry in Translation is the only UK magazine dedicated solely to poetry in translation.

item.title: Kill Your Darlings: minimum $1,000 for short fiction
item.description: Kill Your Darlings pays a minimum of $1,000 for short fiction of 2,000–5,000 words, and reads year-round from established and emerging writers.

item.title: Island: closed 18 Sep 2026; graphic narratives open
item.description: Island, a Tasmanian literary and arts magazine, closed its 18 September 2026 windows: print poetry (Island 180), print fiction and nonfiction, and all three

item.title: Hinterland: pays for all published creative non-fiction
item.description: Hinterland publishes creative non-fiction of 500–5,000 words and pays for all the work it publishes, though it does not state a rate.

item.title: High Country News: $1 a word for reported content
item.description: High Country News pays $1 per word for reported content and 50 cents per word for essays and reviews, at the same rate whether the work runs in print, online

item.title: Gutter: flat £50 per piece, Scottish and
item.description: Gutter is a magazine of new Scottish and international writing paying a flat £50 per published piece regardless of length or style.

item.title: Granta submissions: open 1–30 September 2026
item.description: Granta is open to unsolicited fiction and non-fiction during four month-long windows a year — the current one closes 30 September 2026.

item.title: Geist: up to $650 for features, $100 per page for poetry
item.description: Geist, a Canadian magazine of ideas and culture, pays up to $650 for longform essays, fiction and comics, $100 per page for poetry, and $100–300 for short

item.title: FreeFall Magazine
item.description: FreeFall Magazine, based in Calgary, pays $10 per published page for prose to a maximum of $100, $25 per poem, and $50 for interviews and book reviews, plus a

item.title: fourteen poems: £30 per poem, open for Issue 21
item.description: fourteen poems publishes an anthology of LGBTQ+ poetry around three times a year and pays £30 for each poem published. Submissions are open for Issue 21.

item.title: Extra Teeth: £200 per piece, next window 1–14 December 2026
item.description: Extra Teeth is a Scottish magazine paying £200 for each piece selected for the print magazine and £150 for its Substack. Pieces run 800–4,000 words.

item.title: EVENT: $40 per page for poetry, $35 for prose, up to $500
item.description: EVENT pays $40 per page for poetry and book reviews and $35 per page for prose, up to a maximum of $500, plus two copies.
